name: Henry Hallett Dale
summary: British physiologist and pharmacologist known for work on chemical transmission of nerve impulses.

name: Henry Wellcome
summary: American-born British pharmaceutical entrepreneur and founder of Burroughs, Wellcome & Co.

name: Walter Dowson
summary: Director of the Wellcome Physiological Research Laboratories during the 1906 dispute.

name: Hooper Jowett
summary: Distinguished chemist and deputy to Frederick Power at the Wellcome Chemical Research Laboratories.

name: Frederick Power
summary: Distinguished chemist and Director of the Wellcome Chemical Research Laboratories.

name: Burroughs, Wellcome & Co.
summary: British pharmaceutical firm known for ethical pharmacy and scientific research laboratories.

name: Wellcome Physiological Research Laboratories
summary: Research laboratory established by Henry Wellcome for physiological and pharmacological research.

name: Wellcome Chemical Research Laboratories
summary: Research laboratory established by Henry Wellcome for chemical research and analysis.

name: Parke, Davis & Co.
summary: American pharmaceutical firm that registered the trademark 'Adrenalin'.

name: Journal of Physiology
summary: Scientific journal where Dale intended to publish his 1906 paper on ergot.

aliases: Professor of Physiology at University College London
name: Ernest Starling
summary: Professor of Physiology at University College London who advised Wellcome on hiring Dale.

name: T R Elliott
summary: Physiologist who collaborated with Dale and published a definitive paper on adrenaline action.

aliases: Editor of the Journal of Physiology
name: J N Langley
summary: Editor of the Journal of Physiology and eminent physiologist at Cambridge.

name: Alfred Chune Fletcher
summary: Medico-legal expert and close friend and adviser of Henry Wellcome.

name: John Jacob Abel
summary: American pharmacologist who proposed the name 'epinephrin' for the suprarenal extract.

name: Jokichi Takamine
summary: Industrial chemist who developed purification techniques for adrenaline and patented them.

name: Adrenalin
summary: Registered trademark of Parke, Davis & Co. for the active principle of the suprarenal gland.
